Exercise E.1 — Discounted sums, horizons and time constants
      
      
        Rewards satisfy $|r|\le2$ and $\gamma=0.95$. (a) Bound $|G|$ for every trajectory. (b) After how many steps does the weight $\gamma^T$ drop below $1\%$? (c) The discrete steps are samples every $0.1$ s of a continuous-time problem with weight $e^{-t/\tau}$. Which time constant $\tau$ (in seconds) corresponds to $\gamma=0.95$? (d) Bound the part of the return earned after the $T$ of (b).
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) $|G|\le\sum_t0.95^t\cdot2=2/0.05=40$.
            (b) $0.95^T\le0.01\iff T\ge\ln100/\ln(1/0.95)=4.6052/0.05129=89.8$, so $T=90$ (check: $0.95^{89}=0.0104$, $0.95^{90}=0.0099$). Compare $1/(1-\gamma)=20$: about $4.6$ time constants.
            (c) $\gamma=e^{-\Delta t/\tau}$ with $\Delta t=0.1$ s gives $\tau=-\Delta t/\ln\gamma=0.1/0.05129=1.95$ s, i.e. $19.5$ steps, close to $1/(1-\gamma)=20$.
            (d) $\big|\sum_{t\ge90}\gamma^tr_t\big|\le\gamma^{90}\cdot2/(1-\gamma)=0.0099\cdot40=0.40$: at most $1\%$ of the worst-case total.
